photos.title: Sanktuarium Afrodyty
photos.author: xiquinhosilva
photos.description:
The Roman Sanctuary of the Paphian Aphrodite, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Cyprus, is an ancient sanctuary dedicated to the goddess Aphrodite, marking the legendary site of her birthplace. Originating in the Late Bronze Age around the 12th century BC, it served as a major center of worship for fertility deities and later the Greek and Roman cult of Aphrodite for over two millennia until the 4th century AD. 
Its ruins feature foundation walls, Roman-period structures, and sacred artifacts, offering exceptional testimony to the continuity of religious practices and cultural exchange in the ancient Mediterranean.

photos.title: Sanktuarium Afrodyty
photos.author: xiquinhosilva
photos.description:
The Roman Sanctuary of the Paphian Aphrodite, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Cyprus, is an ancient sanctuary dedicated to the goddess Aphrodite, marking the legendary site of her birthplace. Originating in the Late Bronze Age around the 12th century BC, it served as a major center of worship for fertility deities and later the Greek and Roman cult of Aphrodite for over two millennia until the 4th century AD. 
Its ruins feature foundation walls, Roman-period structures, and sacred artifacts, offering exceptional testimony to the continuity of religious practices and cultural exchange in the ancient Mediterranean.
photos.caption: Ruiny sanktuarium Afrodyty w Palaipafos, widok ogólny; kadr z 8 października 2025.
photos.alt: Kamienne fundamenty i kolumny sanktuarium na trawiastym płaskowyżu.

photos.title: Zejście do grobowca 2
photos.author: Punteador
photos.description: The stepped passage (dromos) cut into the rock and leading down to the entrance of Tomb 2 at the Tombs of the Kings, Paphos. The Tombs of the Kings is a large necropolis about 2 km north of Paphos harbour (Cyprus); its underground tombs, many dating back to the 4th century BC, are carved out of solid rock. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1980, together with Nea Paphos and Palaepaphos.
